title: Alpha rollup: define minimal card contracts, dependency gating, and acceptance matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures the product decision to aggressively trim the alpha Console surface for the upcoming Q2 alpha launch. The aim is to ship a tightly scoped dashboard+tracing+cost-summary experience that demonstrates end-to-end value while deferring higher-cost telemetry and deep-cost-explorer features. This document defines the minimal card contracts, gating rules for dependent engineering work, explicit scope cuts, and an acceptance matrix that will be used for the alpha canary rollout.

Background & motivation:
- Customer research shows early adopters need concise route-level cost visibility, basic slow-path tracing, and a single pane for SLO regressions. Full-fidelity heatmaps and per-token cost attribution drive high infra/observability costs and can be deferred.
- Platform constraints: analytics ingestion budget limited for alpha; runtime team has capacity for two small runtime API changes (trace sampling param + route-level cost aggregation).

Alpha objectives (what we must ship):
1) A compact Insights Card set (max 4 cards) showing small summary metrics for routes: 7d cost, 7d calls, p95 latency, error rate.
2) A lightweight Traces inspector that surfaces sampled request traces with anchor to the route and simple waterfall view (no distributed trace correlation).
3) A Cost Summary tile that shows per-route spend (top 10 routes) and delta vs prior week with quick filter by environment (prod/staging).
4) Basic rollout telemetry: event when a user opens console, views a card, and clicks to expand trace.

Explicit scope cuts (deferred from alpha):
- Remove per-token cost heatmap and token-level attribution (defer to Beta).
- Defer expensive full-trace aggregation (no distributed joins, no long tail trace aggregation).
- No advanced drilldowns or multi-card cross-filtering in alpha (cards are independent).
- No on-demand heavy sampling or long-retention trace storage (short 7d retention for sampled traces only).

Minimal card contracts (interfaces & constraints):
- Card metadata: {route_id, route_name, env, time_window}. (Interface intentionally minimal; implementation teams to accept JSON with these keys).
- Payload size: single card payload must be < 60KB compressed for alpha.
- Response latency: backend must return card payload within 400ms p95 for local console requests (see acceptance criteria).

Gating and dependencies:
- ENG-78234: analytics-aggregation-pipeline — must deliver route-level 7d cost rollup by 2026-03-14 (gated).
- ENG-45678: trace-sampling-param — runtime API to expose sample_rate override per project by 2026-03-21 (gated).
- DES-3401: compact-card-visuals — design tokens and 4 card composables due 2026-03-07.
- Security: integrate audit event for Console reads (low priority for alpha but basic audit event required).

Rollout plan (canary -> alpha):
- Canary dim: internal + 5 pilot customers (feature-flagged). Verify costs & perf for 72h.
- Alpha: open to wider org plus opt-in customers after canary signoff.
- Beta: restore deferred scopes progressively (heatmaps, cross-filtering, longer retention).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: observability costs spike due to naive sampling. Mitigation: enforce default sample_rate 0.02 for alpha; engineering to enforce cap.
- Risk: slow card responses during peak hours. Mitigation: priority routing to dedicated aggregation nodes for alpha and a circuit breaker to hide the card with a friendly fallback message.

Links & artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Alpha+Rollup+PRD
- Design comps: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-alpha-card-comps
- Engineering spec (analytics): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/123
- Sample dashboard mock: https://app.mockingbird.example/alpha-console-snapshot
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Insights surface includes no more than 4 cards; each card populated for >90% of test routes in pilot dataset
AC-2: Cost Summary tile returns top-10 route spend within 500ms median and 1s p95 for pilot canary users
AC-3: Traces inspector opens sampled traces and displays waterfall within 750ms p95; no distributed correlation links required for alpha
AC-4: Sampling and caps applied: default sample_rate <= 0.02; engineering validation of enforcement present in canary logs
AC-5: Telemetry events emitted for open_card, expand_trace, and open_cost_summary; events flow to analytics sink for pilot customers
AC-6: Circuit-breaker fallback triggers on backend latency > 1.2s and surfaces a clear product message explaining degraded mode
AC-7: Security: Console read audit events emitted to the cluster audit log for alpha deployments
decisions: D1: Defer per-token attribution and heatmap until Beta to control ingestion costs
D2: Limit cards to independent summaries (no cross-filtering) to reduce backend fan-out and complexity
D3: Require analytics rollup (ENG-78234) as a hard gate before canary to prevent expensive on-demand aggregation
D4: Use conservative default sampling (0.02) and enforce server-side cap to avoid burst cost growth
